recipes.name: Masoor Dal with Spinach
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in fiber, which may benefit triglyceride management and support healthy cholesterol levels. Spinach provides iron, which could contribute to optimal hemoglobin levels, and Vitamin B12 from the dal helps in red blood cell formation.
instructions: Wash masoor dal thoroughly and soak for 15-20 minutes.
Heat ghee/oil in a pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for another minute.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, red chili, and coriander powder. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Drain the dal and add it to the cooker along with chopped spinach. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add water and salt. Close the lid and pressure cook for 3-4 whistles.
Once pressure releases, mash the dal lightly if desired. Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Pulao
recipes.health_benefit: This balanced meal provides lean protein from chicken, essential for muscle maintenance and satiety, which may aid in blood sugar management. The mixed vegetables add fiber and micronutrients, while brown rice offers complex carbohydrates to support stable energy levels.
instructions: Wash and soak brown rice for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds and whole spices. Sauté for a few seconds.
Add sliced onions and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute.
Add diced chicken and cook until it changes color. Add turmeric, coriander, and garam masala powders. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add mixed vegetables and soaked brown rice. Gently mix for 2 minutes.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes (or pressure cook for 2 whistles on medium heat).
Once cooked, let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork. Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve hot with dahi (yogurt).

recipes.name: Palak Paneer
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is a good source of calcium from paneer and iron from spinach, supporting bone health and optimal hemoglobin levels. The protein content may contribute to satiety and balanced blood sugar, while the fiber from spinach could aid digestive health and triglyceride management.
instructions: Blanch spinach in hot water for 2-3 minutes, then immediately plunge into cold water to retain color. Drain and blend into a smooth paste.
Heat oil/ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, sauté for a minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomato, turmeric, and coriander powder. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add the spinach paste and cook for 5-7 minutes on medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Add paneer cubes, garam masala, and salt. Mix gently and simmer for another 3-5 minutes.
If desired, stir in a tablespoon of fresh cream just before serving.
Serve hot with whole wheat roti or brown rice.

recipes.name: Fish Curry (Rohu/Salmon)
recipes.health_benefit: Fatty fish like rohu or salmon are excellent sources of Omega-3 fatty acids, which are crucial for maintaining healthy HDL levels and managing triglycerides. This recipe provides high-quality protein and essential Vitamin D, contributing to overall cardiovascular and bone health.
instructions: Clean and wash fish pieces. Marinate lightly with salt and a pinch of turmeric.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Let them splutter.
Add curry leaves, green chilies, and chopped onion. Sauté until onion is golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until fragrant.
Add tomato purée and cook until oil separates. Stir in turmeric, red chili, and coriander powders. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add tamarind pulp (or kokum) and 1-1.5 cups of water. Bring to a simmer.
Gently place the fish pieces into the simmering curry. If using, add coconut milk now.
Cover and cook on low heat for 7-10 minutes, or until fish is cooked through. Avoid overcooking.
Adjust salt to taste. Garnish with fresh coriander.
Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Salad
recipes.health_benefit: This refreshing salad is packed with fiber and plant-based protein, which may contribute to better blood sugar control and satiety, supporting a healthy weight. Sprouts enhance nutrient absorption and provide a good source of B vitamins and Vitamin C, which aids iron absorption.
instructions: Ensure moong dal is well-sprouted (can be bought pre-sprouted or homemade by soaking dal overnight and then letting it sprout for 1-2 days).
In a bowl, combine sprouted moong dal, chopped cucumber, tomato, onion (if using), green chili, and coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt.
Mix everything thoroughly. Taste and adjust seasonings if needed.
Serve fresh as a healthy snack or a light side dish.

recipes.name: Oats Dalia Upma with Mixed Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: This breakfast provides a sustained energy release due to complex carbohydrates and high fiber content from oats and dalia, which may help manage blood glucose levels and support healthy cholesterol. The added vegetables enhance micronutrient intake, contributing to overall vitality.
instructions: Dry roast oats and dalia separately until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and curry leaves, let them splutter.
Add chopped onion, green chili, and grated ginger. Sauté until onion turns translucent.
Add mixed vegetables and turmeric powder. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender-crisp.
Add roasted oats and dalia, mix well.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until all water is absorbed and oats/dalia are cooked (about 8-10 minutes).
Fluff with a fork. Squeeze lemon juice before serving.
Serve hot.

recipes.name: Besan Cheela with Paneer Bhurji (egg-free)
recipes.health_benefit: This protein-rich breakfast provides a good source of fiber from besan (chickpea flour), which may aid in blood sugar management and contribute to a feeling of fullness. Paneer offers calcium and protein, supporting bone health and muscle maintenance without using eggs.
instructions: For Cheela: In a bowl, whisk besan with water to form a smooth batter (similar to dosa batter). Add chopped onion, capsicum, green chili, coriander leaves, turmeric, cumin powder, and salt. Mix well. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
For Paneer Bhurji: Heat 1 tsp oil in a separate pan. Add ginger-garlic paste, then chopped tomato and sauté until soft. Add crumbled paneer and a pinch of salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Keep aside.
Heat a non-stick tawa. Lightly grease it. Pour a ladleful of cheela batter and spread evenly into a thin circle.
Cook on medium heat until edges crisp and bottom is golden. Flip and cook the other side.
Place some paneer bhurji in the center of the cooked cheela, fold it, and serve immediately.
Repeat for the remaining batter.
